unfold.unfolded: Conjecture. Assume that $G$ is simply laced. Let $g\in G_{\geqslant 0}$ and let $H=Z_G(g_s)$, where $g_s$ and $g_u$ are the semisimple and unipotent parts of $g$. Then there exists a weak pinning $\underline{\mathbf P_H}$ of $H$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $g_u\in H_{\underline{\mathbf P_H},\geqslant 0}$; \item $V(g,c_M)_{\underline{\mathbf P_H},\geqslant 0}=V(g,c_M)\cap V_{\geqslant 0}$ for any irreducible representation $V$ of $G$. \end{enumerate}
notes: G_{≥0}, c_M, V(g,c_M), H_{P,≥0} and V_{≥0} are not defined in the context, so they are kept as the paper writes them.
The word Conjecture at the start marks the kind of the item and is not part of the statement.
The context does not say whether the irreducible representations are finite dimensional, so the statement is kept without that condition.

verdict.reason: The unfolded form preserves both hypotheses and both conclusions. It only clarifies that $g_s$ and $g_u$ denote the semisimple and unipotent parts of $g$.
